run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Social Network
Namespace: social-network

A social network with unidirectional follow relationships, implemented with loosely-coupled microservices, communicating with each other via Thrift RPCs.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The social-network namespace and all 27 Deployments were created by helm at 2026-11-24T03:41:00 (namespace created 03:40:59), so the observable history covers only the last ~25 s of the authorized window. The business request path looked healthy in that sample: nginx-web-server /wrk2-api/post/compose, /wrk2-api/home-timeline/read and /wrk2-api/user-timeline/read all returned http.status_code=200 with no error spans and sub-9 ms latencies (03:41:09-03:41:24), and 26 of 27 Deployments had 1/1 ready replicas. The one broken workload is the tracing Deployment jaeger: it was applied separately by kubectl-client-side-apply at 03:41:08 with replicas=2, a single ReadWriteOnce openebs-hostpath claim (jaeger-pvc, PV pinned by nodeAffinity to sregym-worker) and a required podAntiAffinity on kubernetes.io/hostname. One replica runs on sregym-worker holding the volume; the second pod jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-6sg2t is permanently Pending (PodScheduled=False, reason Unschedulable: anti-affinity on one node, control-plane taint, volume node affinity conflict on the other two), with FailedScheduling Warning events at 03:41:11 and 03:41:16. Deployment status is 2 desired / 1 available. This jaeger Deployment is not on the app request path (services export to otel-collector.observe.svc.cluster.local and the jaeger-* Services are ExternalName to it), so no business-service impact was observed. Separately, and not linked to jaeger, social-graph-service logged 'GetFollowers user_id: N not found' for every sampled GetFollowers call from 03:41:10 to 03:41:25 because its MongoDB collection social-graph.social-graph was created empty at 03:41:07; user.user and post.post were likewise created empty, so home-timeline reads return 200 with empty content. Whether that missing social-graph data is an injected fault or simply an unseeded fresh install could not be determined. Overall conclusion is partial: the jaeger scheduling fault is established, the app-data gap and the identity of any reported incident remain unresolved.

claims.text: Deployment jaeger in namespace social-network was created/applied at 2026-11-24T03:41:08 by manager kubectl-client-side-apply (not by the 03:41:00 helm install of the other 26 Deployments) with spec.replicas=2, a persistentVolumeClaim volume jaeger-volume -> jaeger-pvc, and requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution podAntiAffinity on topologyKey kubernetes.io/hostname for label service=jaeger; its status shows replicas=2 with readyReplicas=1 and availableReplicas=1.

Pod jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-6sg2t (owner ReplicaSet jaeger-9fd7cdb7c, created 03:41:08) is Pending with node=null and condition PodScheduled=False reason=Unschedulable, message: '0/4 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match pod anti-affinity rules, 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: }, 2 node(s) had volume node affinity conflict.'

Warning FailedScheduling events were recorded inside the authorized window for pod jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-6sg2t at 2026-11-24T03:41:11 and 03:41:16, naming pod anti-affinity, the control-plane taint and unavailable/affinity-conflicting persistent volumes.

PersistentVolumeClaim jaeger-pvc is Bound with accessModes ReadWriteOnce, storageClassName openebs-hostpath and volumeName pvc-2c730a74-3163-4c1e-a676-d1044b59f9d4; that PersistentVolume carries required nodeAffinity kubernetes.io/hostname In [sregym-worker], so the volume can only be mounted on node sregym-worker.

The sibling pod jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-q8m74 is Running and Ready on node sregym-worker with restartCount 0 and a running container, so the running jaeger replica and its volume mount work; the failure is that the Deployment's second replica cannot be placed.

Of the 27 Deployments in namespace social-network, jaeger is the only one with desired replicas 2 and only 1 ready/available (status replicas 2, ready 1); every other Deployment reports replicas=1, ready=1, available=1.

The in-namespace jaeger Deployment is not on the application request path: the services' jaeger-config.yml sets reporter.localAgentHostPort to otel-collector.observe.svc.cluster.local:6831, and Services jaeger, jaeger-agent, jaeger-collector and jaeger-query in social-network are ExternalName services pointing to otel-collector.observe.svc.cluster.local.

Sampled spans of the business paths 03:41:09-03:41:24 show success: 16 nginx-web-server /wrk2-api/home-timeline/read spans with http.status_code=200 (794-2314 us), 8 /wrk2-api/user-timeline/read root/child spans with http.status_code=200 (1772-3034 us), and a /wrk2-api/post/compose trace with http.status_code=200 (8.5-8.7 ms) in which compose-post-service, text-service, user-mention-service, url-shorten-service, post-storage-service, social-graph-service, home-timeline-service and user-timeline-service spans all carry no error status.

social-graph-service logged '<warning>: (SocialGraphHandler.h:612:GetFollowers) user_id: N not found' for every GetFollowers call in the sample: the count of lines matching 'GetFollowers' and the count matching 'not found' are the same 160 lines between 03:41:10 and 03:41:25, and the only non-'not found' lines from that pod in 03:41:00-03:41:25 are its startup lines and two MongoDB index-creation errors.

social-graph-mongodb created collection social-graph.social-graph (and index user_id_1) at 03:41:07 with uuidDisposition 'generated', i.e. the collection did not exist before; user-mongodb likewise created user.user at 03:41:04 and post-storage-mongodb created post.post at 03:41:05 with generated UUIDs. The social-network namespace itself was created 2026-11-24T03:40:59Z.

All four nodes (sregym-control-plane, sregym-worker, sregym-worker2, sregym-worker3) are Ready with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure all False, and all 26 non-jaeger Service/Endpoints pairs in social-network have populated addresses (including nginx-thrift 10.244.7.239:8080 and social-graph-service 10.244.7.210:9090).

Primary candidate cause: Deployment jaeger's own settings - 2 replicas combined with required host-level pod anti-affinity and one ReadWriteOnce openebs-hostpath volume pinned to sregym-worker - make the second replica permanently unschedulable; the fault originates in that Deployment object applied at 03:41:08, and its only observable effect is the degraded jaeger Deployment (1 of 2 available) and the Pending pod, because application tracing is exported to otel-collector.observe instead.

Second candidate: the social-graph dataset is absent, so GetFollowers finds no user for every request and the home-timeline read path returns empty content while still answering HTTP 200. Because every application datastore (user.user, post.post, social-graph.social-graph) was created empty within 8 seconds of the install, no seeding Job or CronJob exists in the namespace, and no object was seen applying this condition, it is equally possible that this is simply the unseeded state of a freshly installed environment; it is not shown to be caused by the jaeger Deployment.

No application-level error or latency signal was observed: no span in the 03:41:09-03:41:24 sample carries an error status or a non-200 HTTP status, no /wrk2-api span exceeded 500 ms, and the only log lines matching error/fail/warn/not-found patterns in the window from business services were MongoDB connection races during startup (03:41:02-03:41:06, e.g. user-service 'Error in createIndexes: No suitable servers found' on user-mongodb:27017), which stopped once the databases came up.

Rejected: the Pending jaeger pod is a crashed or restarting container. jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-6sg2t has no containerStatuses at all (never scheduled) and its sibling jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-q8m74 is Running/Ready with restartCount 0, so the failure is scheduling, not container failure.

Rejected: an application-wide outage during the window. Probes to all 13 blackbox-social-network targets returned probe_success=0 at 03:39:30-03:41:00, but that is before the social-network namespace and its Deployments existed (created 03:40:59-03:41:00); from 03:41:09 the request paths answer 200 and every non-jaeger Deployment reports 1/1 ready, so the zero probes are install timing, not an app outage.

Make the jaeger workload schedulable: set Deployment jaeger replicas to 1 (its current usable state), or move it to a volume that can be mounted on more than one node (ReadWriteMany) and/or drop the required kubernetes.io/hostname podAntiAffinity, since jaeger-pvc/PV is bound to sregym-worker and a second jaeger pod is forbidden on that host.

Clarify whether the social graph and user/post datasets are expected to be pre-loaded: if so, verify/execute the initialization that populates social-graph.social-graph (and user.user) and confirm that GetFollowers stops logging 'user id not found'; consider an alert on the social-graph-service 'not found' warning rate, since this failure is invisible to HTTP status and to the existing error-rate/latency alerts.

gaps: No application history exists to compare against: the social-network namespace was created 2026-11-24T03:40:59Z and every workload 03:41:00-03:41:08, and the only cadvisor sample for the namespace falls at 03:41:25, so metrics/traces/logs for this app before 03:41 are unknown (not zero).

No traces_span_metrics_calls_total or traces_span_metrics_duration series existed in the authorized window: the queries for those metrics, the service_name label values, and the blackbox probe_success series over the long window all returned no_data inside the window, so app error-rate and latency trends before 03:41:25 are unknown and the HighRequestErrorRate/HighRequestLatency rules could not be evaluated for the window.
The change_history integration is not configured, so what or who applied the jaeger manifest at 03:41:08 (kubectl-client-side-apply) and whether any earlier change existed could not be verified.

Whether the missing social-graph data (GetFollowers 'user not found') is an injected fault or the expected state of an unseeded fresh install is unresolved; no seeding Job/CronJob and no object applying that condition was found in social-network.

The PendingPodsDetected/PodSchedulingFailure alert history and pod state were read at 03:42-03:45, i.e. after the authorized window end (03:41:25), so only the 03:41:11/03:41:16 FailedScheduling events prove the in-window state.
The Redis integration was unavailable (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on redis_info/redis_scan_keys), so the contents of social-graph-redis and home-timeline-redis could not be checked directly.

The social-graph-service log read was limited (incomplete: newest 100 of 165 matching lines shown), so the full run of 'not found' warnings before 03:41:15 was not enumerated; the counts cited come from the Loki count_over_time series over 03:40:00-03:41:25.

Log reads of the nginx-thrift and jaeger pods returned no lines in the window, and the in-cluster persistentvolume query matched nothing under the exact name queried, so front-end proxy logs and the PV object as a whole remain unverified.
secret values in the service-config.json ConfigMaps are redacted, so no conclusion depends on them and they could not be verified.
next_steps: Fix the jaeger Deployment placement: reduce replicas to 1 or provide a storage class/access mode and affinity rules that allow the second replica (or remove the required host anti-affinity), then confirm the Deployment reports 2/2 available and no Pending pod remains.

Verify how the DeathStarBench social graph, users and posts are supposed to be seeded in this environment; if a seeding step exists, run it and re-check social-graph-service for 'GetFollowers ... not found' and confirm home-timeline reads return posts.
Add a signal for the silent GetFollowers 'user not found' condition (log-based alert or a metric on social-graph-service lookups) because it does not produce HTTP errors or increased latency.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

view.cannot_prove: A line that is not returned is unknown, not proof that nothing was logged: only limit lines are shown (the newest), and retention, ingest delay, the label selector and line filters can leave gaps. The timestamp is when the line was ingested or parsed, not necessarily when the event happened. A metric query counts only lines inside the query window.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
